Hi Daniel —

On Tue, Aug 21, 2028 Daniel Park wrote: > Thanks for taking this RFP... (see original)

Attached is a compact answer set (RNWD_Perf_Appendix_ANSWERS.pdf) plus links to the run artifacts. Below is a high-level summary and the specific data we think directly addresses your questions. If you'd like more raw traces we'll upload sample logs (per your consent) after the soak run.

1) Test harness and traffic synthesis- We use an internal runner (runner-sim v1.3) that can replay request mixes at token level. Configs are deterministic (seeded RNG) and live in the attached artifacts (traffic-config.json inside the Drive folder). For headroom runs we ramp concurrency in steps (1,2,4,8,16,32,64) holding each step for a 120s steady-state window; for soak we run sustained at target concurrency for 1 hour.

2) Definitions: cold vs warm- Cold start: first request against a freshly-initialized model worker where no KV/prefix cache or JIT kernels are warm. Measured from request arrival to model response. Warm start: subsequent requests when KV cache and kernels are loaded; measured after N=10 warmup requests. We provide the measurement script (measure_startup.py) with the PDF.

3) Representative numbers (sample model: rdw-30b-8k-quant, 32k batch token budget):
- Single replica, p4d instance type, concurrency=8: median=34ms, p95=98ms, p99=190ms
- Single replica, concurrency=32: aggregate throughput ~75 req/s, median=85ms, p95=210ms, p99=420ms
- With prefix/KV cache hit ratio >90% (multi-tenant warm): p50 improves ~25%, p95 improves ~30%
These are representative lab figures; we include full CSVs in the Drive link.

4) Scaling behavior & replica strategy- Throughput scales near-linearly until queueing effects dominate; practical inflection points vary by model size and token length. Autoscaling trigger: sustained p95 latency above configured SLO or GPU compute queuing > 60% for 30s. We recommend a conservative target of keeping p95 < 250ms for conversational workloads; our dedicated customers typically size to allow 20-30% headroom.

5) Tail-latency decomposition and mitigation- We decompose observed tail into: kernel jitter, DRAM page faults (runtime), KV miss penalty, and scheduling queueing. Mitigations we use: dynamic batching caps, prefix caching, kernel pre-warm, and graceful fallback to lower-precision variants when p99 > threshold. The PDF has a waterfall chart from a representative run.

6) Multi-tenant isolation and cache effects- Prefix/KV caches are per-tenant in Dedicated; in hosted environments we provide tenant-aware cache namespaces. Measurement method: compare baseline runs with synthetic tenant churn to runs with pinned session affinity. We provide scripts to reproduce.

7) Quantization and kernel variability- Quantized variants reduce GPU memory and improve throughput; however, p99 tail can widen if kernel fallback occurs. Our lab harness tracks kernel selection events and we attach a sample trace.

Artifacts included:
- RNWD_Perf_Appendix_ANSWERS.pdf (narrative + figures)
- CSVs: scaling-curves-rdw-30b.csv, p99-breakdown.csv
- soak-test-plan.yaml (draft)
- sample-run raw logs: soak-test-raw-logs-sample.tar.gz (anonymized)

Drive link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2B3cPerfArtifacts

If you want, we can run a short 1-hour soak during Aug 25–26; we'll need a short window for credentials and a minimal IP allowlist so we can upload logs to your bucket. Proposed contact for the run: perf@redwoodinference.com (we'll pull logs to the Drive folder and tag them to your deal id).

Happy to walk through the PDF live — propose 30m on Aug 25 if that works.

Cheers,

Markus Klein

Hi Daniel —

Quick answers inline: 
- Dataset: the representative numbers above are from our synthetic seed set aligned to an 80/20 short/long prompt distribution; we can switch to your supplied prompt set for the soak — please upload a gzipped sample and we'll replay it verbatim.
- Cache isolation: for hosted tenants we use tenant-scoped cache namespaces and soft eviction policies; while noisy neighbors can affect wall-clock hit ratios, our metrics show isolation keeps per-tenant hit ratio degradation under 10% in stress scenarios. For strict isolation we recommend Dedicated (tenant-private caches).
- Logs: our standard run artifacts include per-request kernel-selection events, GPU memory delta traces (sampled at 1s), and full per-request latency/queueing fields. We can push the raw logs directly to your S3 bucket — please share a pre-signed upload or short-lived IAM role; otherwise we'll place the artifacts in the Drive folder.

I've attached the soak-test-plan.yaml (draft) and set the proposed window for Aug 25 09:00–10:00 PDT. We will: warm 15 minutes, run 45 minutes at target concurrency, and then capture 15m of cool-down traces. Post-run we'll upload the anonymized raw logs to your bucket.

If that schedule works, please send the S3 upload details and we'll lock it in.

Best regards,

Markus Klein
Performance Lead, Redwood Inference
